utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue with the cross-examination of the witness, I'd first like to deal with a few procedural matters. The first one being that the Defence has requested an extension of time to file Rule 94 bis notice, notices for proposed experts. The Prosecution did not oppose but requested the Defence to ensure that this extension does not cause delays in the hearing of scheduled witnesses. The extension request is granted, but the Defence is urged to file its notices as soon as possible so as to avoid any delays in the hearing of upcoming witnesses. We should have delivered this decision last Friday, because that's when the time limit elapsed, but that is done here by -- although half an hour late. Then, Mr. Groome, I think Ms. Bolton wished to make submissions for ten minutes on certain matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We were waiting to hear from the Chamber when you would hear her. If you advise me, I will make sure she's here in court for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And how much time would that approximately take, because I have a few matters, and there are a few other matters, I think, also in relation to Witness Fraser. Three documents still to be addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think it would be difficult to bring her down right now, Your Honour, but maybe the beginning of next session or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first see how we deal with the next witness -- with the present witness and let's see when, but if she could be available later this morning then that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then MFI P6, Security Council Resolution. I think the Defence wanted to indicate its position. That's at least what we were told a few days ago, on the revised version of this document. Are there any objections against the revised version of this Security Council Resolution? I think it's for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have had a look at it and considered the matter, Your Honours, and we don't have any objections to this amended -- or, rather, revised version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the new version may replace the old one. It has been uploaded into e-court. Madam Registrar, are you aware of the new upload in relation to MFI P6?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I'm not aware of the number, but I will receive it from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it possible to give it right away? Then we can finalise the matter. But the one which has been uploaded, the number still to be verified, may replace the old version, and the Registry is instructed to do so. The new version then is admitted into evidence. Madam Registrar, MFIs D65, D67, and D81, these were outstanding translations. Have the translations meanwhile been received?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, for D65, D67, and D81 we have received the translation uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They may be attached to the originals so that we have now originals and translations. D65, D67, and D81 are admitted into evidence. Yes. These were the matters I wished to raise before we continue with the present witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have for the witness who has the protective measures of face distortion, we have to briefly go into closed session to allow the witness to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning, Mr. Miokovic. Before we continue, I have to admit that I'd forgotten to instruct you last Friday that you should not speak with anyone or communicate in any other way with whomever about your testimony. I was informed that at our request, the Victims and Witnesses Section passed on this instruction to you. Could you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can confirm that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, we'll now continue, and I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Stojanovic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd just like to go into some of the details that concern your professional background. If I have understood this correctly, you started working in the police force having completed secondary school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of your work in the police force, did you receive training of any kind in relation to ballistics, artillery, sniper rifles, and other weapons that you may have came across subsequently?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you perform your military service? If so, where and what sort of military education did you receive or military training did you receive?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I performed my military service in 1981 in Pula. I was in the Anti-Aircraft Artillery Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn anything about the technical characteristics and the possibilities of mortar weapons during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for mortar weapons, no. While I was doing my military service, I had no training or no contact with the use of mortar weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When the war broke out in Sarajevo, did you have problems -- any problems in the sense that people were wounded by artillery?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded on the 2nd of June, 1992, but I was not wounded as a result of artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you tell the Chamber where you were wounded and how? What were you wounded by?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded in an armed clash with a criminal group in Sarajevo while I was performing my duties as policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you then sent out of Sarajevo and Bosnia and Herzegovina for treatment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the 7th of April -- or from the 7th of April until the 26th of June, 1993, I was receiving treatment in Germany. I returned to Sarajevo on the 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the examination-in-chief, at one point in time you mentioned certain information. You mentioned the percentage of Croats, Serbs, and the percentage of other groups who according to you in the wartime period worked in the police force of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Where did you obtain this information from? Where did you obtain these percentages from that you made use of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't referring to the police forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I wasn't referring to the wartime period. I was referring exclusively to the security services centre in Sarajevo which is where I worked. I was talking about the period from December 1993, when I first arrived in the CSB, the security services centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's make this clear. The percentage of 20 to 25 per cent, does that include the number of those working in the CSB in Sarajevo, and if so, during which period of time? Is that what this percentage refers to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The CSB in Sarajevo from December 1993, which is when I left the police station in Sarajevo and was transferred to the CSB, up until the time that the Dayton agreement was signed. So in fact, that is the period concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like you to tell us how you obtained that information. Is that official information, information to which we might have access? Could we verify this anywhere?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information is information I obtained on the basis of my own experience, because we all worked in the same building. As to whether this information can be verified, I believe that that is the case, because records were kept at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that this is information you obtained by making your personal assessments? It's not as if you came across this official information in any documents.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, this is my own personal assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also declare yourself to be a Serb at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the beginning of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, I always declared myself to be a Yugoslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question concerned the wartime period when you made these assessments and you assessed the number of non-Bosniak employees, when you assessed what the percentages were, that's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I wasn't calculating percentages of any kind. If you're asking me if I declared myself to be a Serb, then my answer is yes, but my assessment regarding 20, 25 per cent is only an assessment that I made on the basis of my own personal observations and experience. It wasn't arrived at through an analysis of any kind. It wasn't arrived through a detailed analysis of the ethnic composition of the Sarajevo CSB, security services centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That is what I'm persuaded of, and that's what I wanted you to say because the transcript says that that is the percentage you were referring to. But I would now like to have a look at the following document: P609. And while we're waiting for this document to appear on the screen, sir, I would just like to tell you that this in fact is an interview that you gave to investigators from the ICTY on the 14th of November, 1995, and it is -- it has been admitted into evidence in this case, and in response to a question put to you by the investigator concerning your ethnicity, on the 14th of November, 1995, you said something contrary to what you just said. You said that you were a Bosniak. Could you please tell the Chamber how it is that there is such a discrepancy? You can see this on the first page. It's line 5.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it, but I don't know what is problematic here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you explain to the witness where you find a contradiction? If it is that he says I always declared myself Yugoslavia and that you find here that his ethnic origin is Bosnian, I don't know whether that's the same. It may be two different instances, and for official purposes in the former Yugoslavia he may have reported himself as a Yugoslav which does not necessarily contradict that he's here described as of Bosnian ethnic origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, a few minutes ago, you can see this in the transcript, the witness said that in the course of the war, it's line 7, if I can see this clearly -- it's page 7, in fact. The witness said that up until the war, he declared himself to be a Yugoslav, and in the course of the war he declared himself to be of Serbian ethnicity. All I am doing now is trying to clear this up, because on the 14th of November, 1995, in the course of the war according to the information he provided to the ICTY, he declared himself to be a Bosnian, to be of Bosnian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can explain, please do so, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My parents were Serbs. Before the war, I always declared myself to be a Yugoslav. In doing that, I was not disregarding my Serbian origins. I don't see what would be problematic about the fact that I said I am a Bosnian here. I said I was a Bosnia, not a Bosniak. I'm pointing this out for the purpose of the translation, the interpretation. But I don't think that this in any way doesn't leave me with the right to declare myself a Serb or to feel that I am a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I won't delve into that matter. I'd now like to deal with the events that concern Livanjska Street, and this relates to the document. Could we please have a look at paragraph 10 in this document. And while waiting for it to appear, there are just a few matters I would like to go through with you. You were at the on-site investigation on the 8th when the first shell fell; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Livanjska Street I was present at that on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you left the site before the second shell fell; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the following day you went to the site again to carry out an on-site investigation because of the second shell that had fallen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the following day we went to the site to repeat the on-site investigation relating to the first shell, because that's what UNPROFOR had requested. We also wanted to carry out an on-site investigation into the second shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, when did that second shell fall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was about half an hour or 45 minutes after we had left. It was perhaps half an hour after we had left the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And tell us when did you leave the site?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to paragraph 12, it was at 1730 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this because I would like to draw your attention to paragraph 14. Could you tell us when you went to the on-site -- to carry out the on-site investigation on the following day, how many shells fell after you had left the site?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two shells fell. I apologise. Well, that's fine now. I just wanted to see paragraph 14. It's fine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I would like us both to have a look at that paragraph, paragraph 14. And here you say at 1900 hours, at 7.00 p.m. that same evening a second shell fell only 20 metres from the site at which the first shell fell. In this statement, is it true that the conclusion you drew is that one shell fell, not two?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are saying is correct. All I can do is assume that I was referring to the second shell, because it had certain consequences. As for the shell that hit the ground, that was imbedded in the ground, there were no consequences. That shell didn't have any particular effect, which was not the case with the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Here you say the following and this statement was given a year after the event, you say that the shell fell at 7.00 p.m. that evening. Today in the course of the examination-in-chief you said it was about half an hour after you left at 5.30. What in fact is correct? This is what you said here today and in the course of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says here is probably correct given all the time that has passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But this is confusing us, which is why I would like to see Exhibit P611, which has been admitted into evidence. Please have a look at Exhibit P611 now. On the 27th of October, 2010, you provide additional supplemental information to the OTP concerning this event. Could we now look at the following page in the B/C/S version. We have the right page in the English, and in describing the chronology of this event in the Livanjska Street, you say that the second shell fell on Livanjska Street at 17.25, and then the third one fell at 17.30 at number 36. Would you please explain what is closest to the truth? In 1995 you said that it was 7.00 p.m., and then as is in P611, you say that the time reference was between 17.25 and 17.30, and then this morning you said that the time reference was 1800 hours, some 30 minutes after you departed.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't have a problem in explaining this. I'm not trying to wiggle myself out of this but to explain this time difference of one hour, of one hour and a half, I really can't do it now. I can't explain it now given all the time that has passed. It could be due to some technical elements, and if we are interested in the accurate precise time when the second and third shell fell, we could probably refer to the accompanying documents, dispatches, that were sent at the time which would probably point us in the right direction. After all, these were just my statements, my recollections.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But we will agree, won't you, that your statement suffers, if I may say so, from the consequences of the passage of time and that it is not fully precise.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given this time interval and given the time references that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no need to ask that. It's clear that the time references are not completely consistent. It's all in the late afternoon, early evening, but it's not consistent. That's clear, Mr. Stojanovic from the statements, from the answers given by the witness, so there's no need to further explore that at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. We were trying to understand this situation better due to the artillery diaries and so that we could make further comparisons, but all right. Let us go back to P609, please, paragraph 10 of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like for you to provide a detailed explanation for the Court, please. On the 8th of November, having received information that there was shelling and that the first shell fell at Livanjska Street, you went on site, and would you please explain to the Court how it came about that the representatives of UNPROFOR left the on-site investigation, as far as you can recollect?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, it was a routine procedure for the UNPROFOR observers to come to the site and to monitor what we were doing during the on-site investigation. Given that the UNPROFOR teams had better mobility, frequently they would reach the site before us. There were situations where they would do things to change the site and how it looked, which of course created problems for us and for our on-site investigations. Now that you're asking me about this particular instance when UNPROFOR left the site, let me tell you this: Two observers of UNPROFOR came to this site. Some 15 to 20 minutes after them, French UNPROFOR battalion came to the site as well. They were not observers. They were active-duty military personnel. They were not observers. And their commander, via an interpreter, told me that they wanted to conduct the on-site investigation and that their experts would come to carry out the on-site investigation together with us. He left the site, and up until the time we departed, we waited for them to come back. However, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you when you talked to this French soldier or French officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the immediate vicinity of the zero point, which is the point where the shell fell. When I say immediate vicinity, I mean distance up to 10 metres from the place where the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, these two UNPROFOR representatives who had been there before you, did they tamper at all with this site and with the traces of the mortar explosion? Did they touch anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, before the French battalion arrived, one of the two observers who had been there, I saw him at one point kneeling close to the zero point, crouching there, and I saw him touching, almost touching, the stabiliser of the shell, and I warned him not to touch it until all the necessary steps had been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that before you started the on-site investigation or after that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at paragraph 10 of your statement. It says there that upon returning to the site having talked to this French soldier whose name you don't know, and you were told that one of the UNPROFOR representatives had tried to pull out the remains of the shell from the ground and that it was one of your people who warned him not to do it, and you are telling us that you told him that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am fully certain that I said this to this UNPROFOR representative who was from Africa. He was a black man. And I'm sure that I told him. And as I said to you, it frequently happened that the UNPROFOR observers would make our work much more difficult by tampering with the evidence at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at item 13, paragraph 13. That evening at around 8.00 p.m., you say in your statement that UNPROFOR held a press conference and that their spokesperson said that the Bosnian police did not let them carry out the on-site investigation and that that evening the minister of the interior issued an order that a report be prepared because this is what the Presidency of the country had asked for, and you personally did that. Now, please tell me, from this time distance can you now explain to us and to the Court where did this statement on UNPROFOR come from? How come the UNPROFOR complained that you did not let them carry out the on-site investigation if the things unfolded in the way that you had just described to us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I confirm that all of this is correct. That's exactly how it was. So then and now, under oath I state that the assertion that the UNPROFOR members were not permitted to carry out an investigation into this event is absolutely untrue, and it's total speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And are you aware that after that UNPROFOR issued another statement in which they said that the shell came from the positions of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that, and this is why the following day there was a joint investigation, if I can name it that, and the dilemma around this position of theirs was cleared up in the technical sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And after you paired up the firing charts of the shells, do you agree that this shell was fired from positions of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know what their official -- and when I say "their" I mean UNPROFOR, what their understanding of the whole thing was, but what I did point out was that when we did pair up the results at the site and when it was noted that the finished charts could not be relevant, they immediately accepted that and even they took the firing tables for the 82-millimetre mortars from our technicians, which was used during the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And since you carried out the inquiry on the 8th and the 9th of -- into the first shelling incident and the second, according to your recollection did they come from the same positions which were under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot be sure until I look at the documents, but I think that they did not. I think that they came from a diametrically opposite direction when you look at the directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me just complete this part of my topic. After you documented your information and operative data and all the investigations that had to do with a certain criminal act, then criminal charges would be submitted to the relevant prosecutor's office once all of that was done. According to what you know, were charges submitted for processing to the relevant prosecutor's office regarding this incident as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about both shelling incidents? I just want to be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We're talking about the same event, but it happened on two different occasions.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the complete documentation along with the criminal charges would be -- and were filed to the relevant prosecutor's office, and if this wasn't done, it would be something unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But what I'm a little bit puzzled about is I have information that your public security centre did not provide the criminal charges to the prosecutor's office for the first shelling incident; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something that simply cannot happen. It cannot happen. Had something like this happened, someone, and in this case it would be me, would be responsible for that. Another reason why this simply could not happen was this: Because of all of this information, all these events regarding the reporting back to UNPROFOR and regarding the assertion that we did not permit them to carry out their investigation, well, the investigation that was carried out on the second day was conducted by the investigating judge of the court in Sarajevo. So in view of this fact in particular, it's practically impossible for this document -- for these documents not to have been provided to the prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you activate your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And this first shelling incident that you talked about when you were at the scene, the investigating judge was not present for that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me about the first day?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the first day.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the law that was in force then about the criminal procedure, it was the duty of the section where I worked to inform immediately the investigating judge on duty as soon as an incident occurred, and then that judge could come to the scene, conduct an investigation or authorise the CSB to carry out the investigation. So on the first day it was this second case. He did not come to the scene, but he authorised us to carry out the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to come back now to this question which was the reason why I put all these other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at 65 ter 12942 in e-court, please. B/C/S page 127, and the English page is page 14 and page 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, we will be looking at the criminal report that was the result of the work of the CSB in Sarajevo, its investigation. The criminal report was submitted on the 21st of December, 1994. Among other things, it is said in the criminal report that: "Based on Article 151 of paragraph 6 of the Law on Criminal Procedure, a criminal report was submitted against unidentified perpetrators due to well founded suspicion that on the 8th of November, 1994, at around 1725 hundred hours," please take note time, "in violation of international law and with intent to kill and inflict physical injuries to as many civilians in the city of Sarajevo as possible, the perpetrators fired two 82-millimetre mortar shells from the north-east direction, from enemy positions at Spicasta Stijena-Hladivode." I'm asking you whether this criminal report is also documentation submitted for the first incident, against the unidentified perpetrators in the first incident.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The criminal report does not refer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then how is that possible? [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How is that possible after you stated here today that you believe there is no doubt that this is something that should have processed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two separate events. This is the second incident. So both in terms of the investigation and in terms of submitting criminal reports, these incidents were treated as separate incidents. So there must be a criminal report that relates to the first shell that killed two children, one directly on the scene and one child died after being taken to the hospital. This criminal report refers exclusively to the incident that occurred after I left the investigation following the impact of the first shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's try to deal with one more question on this topic. The following day, the 9th of November, was there a joint investigation by UNPROFOR and representatives of the CSB Sarajevo that covered both the first shelling incident when one shell dropped there and for the second shelling when two shells fell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am quite sure that a joint investigation was carried out regarding the first incident. It's been a long time since then, so I cannot remember whether an investigation was carried out regarding the second two shells from the second incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please look at P609 again, and can we look at paragraphs 15 and 16. And in paragraph 16, you say that you went with your team to carry out the first investigation for a second time. This was the following day. And when you got there, the UNPROFOR had already completed its investigation. So I'm asking you now, did you conduct this investigation jointly or was it the way that it is stated here, that each of you carried out a separate investigation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the principle was that they carried out their investigation without presenting the results of this investigation to us. After they finished, we would do our investigation, we would get our results, and then these results would be compared. This is what I meant when I said that we worked together, that we did a joint investigation. It wasn't a mixed team. Each team worked independently and then the results were compared.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please now look at paragraph 15, which -- in which you say, among other things, that you established that the same, we're talking about the same, the first mortar shell, was fired from a location that was east of Serb-held positions at Borje. Is this a translation problem, or you stand by what is said here, that somebody said something to you to this effect?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about paragraph 15 here?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, lines two and three.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, regarding the second shelling, we established that the shell came from the east, from Borje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say someone told you, who were you thinking of? Who could have said something like this to you since you do not possess significant expert knowledge as a ballistics expert to be able to tell where the shell came from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this could only have been something that a ballistics expert told us, because it was not my job to conduct any ballistics examinations because I am not an expert in that it wasn't part of my duties to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say east of Borje, would that be the area of Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really -- I really cannot answer this question right now. All I know is that in relation to the place of impact of this shell that we're talking about, Borje and Spicasta Stijena are, conditionally speaking, in the same direction, and what is east of what or west of what, that's something that I'm really not able to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the English language, as far as I'm able to understand it, it's not entirely without ambiguity. It says: "We are certain it was fired from the east, from the locality of Serb-held position at Borje." Now, if you would read from the east, that is from the locality of a Serb-held position at Borje, then you are at Borje. If you read from the east, from the locality, that would mean east of the locality of a Serb-held position of Borje, it is not Borje anymore but it's east of Borje. Now, for me it is a bit unclear in the English and I would like to ask the witness. Did you say that it came from the east, that is from the locality of Serb-held position at Borje, or did you intend to say that it came from a position east in relation to the location of Serb-held position of Borje. That is not Borje, but east of Borje? Which one of the two did you mean, Witness, if you still remember? If you don't remember, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that mortar shell came from the east in relation to the point of impact, but it is also correct that when we read in the B/C/S, it states here east from -- or east of Borje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Borje being more to the west of from where the projectile was fired, the firing position being east of Borje. Is that what you intended to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is exactly the thing that I'm not able to answer. What I want to say is that the mortar shell came from the east in relation to the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. Judge Fluegge may have one more question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, but to a different topic. On page 20, line 3 and 4, you said: "Each team worked independently and then the results were compared." This is in relation to your team and UNPROFOR investigators; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In your statement, which is still on the screen, in paragraph 15 I read there and I quote: "Since it was --" oh, sorry. In another paragraph you said that UNPROFOR didn't disclose their findings to you. Is that also correct? This is paragraph 16 of your statement. The UNPROFOR -- and I quote again: "The UNPROFOR had just completed their investigation but they did not disclose their findings to us by mutual consent." Did they disclose it at a later time or were you able to compare the results of your investigation and the UNPROFOR results?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely, Your Honour. In the other paragraph, paragraph 16 here, this is explained. Thus they first did their measurements. They did not give us the results. After they did that, we did the same, and then we compared these results, and this is explained in this second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That means that UNPROFOR disclosed their results after you have carried out your investigation, but they did it. They disclosed it to you to enable you to compare the results. Is that the right understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you the following in relation to the same matter: On the day it happened, that is the 8th of November, UNPROFOR was around as well and had tried to take any measurements, or did they come for the first time on the 9th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, they did come to the scene on the 8th, but the soldiers came, and they said that their investigation team would come. In spite of the fact that there was a lot of shelling of the broader area where we were, we waited for them but they simply didn't come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what finally made them disclose their results to you? What happened that initially they did not want to share their findings with you and afterwards they did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that we did not quite understand each other. On the first day, the first day, on the 8th of November, UNPROFOR did not carry out an investigation at all. That evening, however, at 2000 hours, it issued a statement that the Bosnian police did not permit them to conduct an investigation. And since I was the leader of the investigation team on the scene, I had to write a statement in relation to that where I wrote down a detailed chronology. Based on the fact that there were two opposing opinions, one that they were not permitted to conduct an investigation and the other that they didn't even attempt to carry it out, it was agreed the investigation be carried out the following day, actually a reconstruction of the incident. The method used to conduct the investigation was that we would conduct separate investigations, and then when each team was finished we would compare our results.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore the nondisclosure of their results was only during the investigations but after you both had completed your investigations you compared the results of your and their investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. And then when we compared the results, they still stood by the position that it's possible that the shot came from the positions of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and when we asked them on the basis of which they went -- reached this conclusion, they said they did it on the basis of these firing tables.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's explained in paragraph 17 of the statement, the use of the different firing tables. Mr. Stojanovic, I think we are at a point where we need to break, but first we should move into closed session in order to allow the witness to leave the courtroom. During the break the curtains can remain down.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Stojanovic, if you would be able to come a bit quicker to the point you want to address, that would certainly be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, before we move on to another event, I would like to deal with two matters. Would I be correct if I said that you can't remember or UNPROFOR members did not carry out an on-site investigation into the second shelling?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember them having carried out such an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there an agreement between the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina and UNPROFOR according to which activities relating to the shelling was co-ordinated as well as the duty that UNPROFOR had to investigate such fatal incidents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything about the officially reached agreements, but on the basis of my experience what I can say is UNPROFOR observers, in 90 per cent of the cases, were always present when we carried out on-site investigations, but UNPROFOR itself very seldom carried out such investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection as far as this site in Livanjska Street is concerned, how far is it from the front line? How far was it from the front line at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite far. It was quite far from the front lines around Sarajevo at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please try to tell the Chamber what the distance would be in hundreds of metres, in kilometres.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three kilometres at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Which ABiH units were deployed at the Kosevo Hill, which is where Livanjska Street is located, if I have understood this correctly.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the wartime period, I was in the police force, and I really don't know anything about the Kosevo Hill or the positions of the ABiH. I don't know which units were present at the various locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But do you remember that during those days there was intensive fighting in that part of the Sarajevo battle-field?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can remember is that the 8th of November was an extremely difficult day -- or, rather, on that day the shelling of Sarajevo was heavy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Which police station did the Kosevo Hill area belong to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Kosevo Hill came under the Centar police station, but during the wartime period the police stations had been divided along territorial lines. They had been broken down into military police stations. As for what the name or designation of the police station at Kosevo Hill was, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How far was the headquarters of the military police station at Kosevo Hill from the site where the shells fell in the street we've been referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several hundred metres, but their headquarters were located far from the sites where the shells hit. The two policemen who were securing the site of the on-site investigation were wounded. They were members of that military police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me now that the police station of the policeman who was wounded was several hundred metres away from the site where he was wounded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now deal with an event that you spoke about on the 3rd of March, 1993, and this relates to the tram that was hit. I'd like to clarify something that was not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at P612, page 6 in the B/C/S version and page 7 in English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a report dated the 3rd of March, 1995, shown to you by the Prosecution, and what I would like to clarify is something that we can see in paragraph 2 of your statement, and there you say, amongst other things, that as soon as information had been received from the high court in Sarajevo Potparic, Milorad was at the head of the on-site investigation, went to the site and carried an investigation there. Do you stand by what you said, that the investigative judge on that occasion went to the site?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it says here, then of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mihajlo Pavlovic, does that name ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know the person. He was a police officer in the Centar police station at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was he present at the on-site investigation as far as you can remember when you and the other individuals mentioned in the report, as well as the investigative judge, went to that site?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. It's not as if he had to be present since he worked in the central police station, and in such cases their task was to go to the site, secure it, and inform us. As to whether he was present at the on-site investigation itself, I really can't remember, but he wasn't officially a member of this on-site investigation team.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who compiles an official report that is part of the criminal file?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the one I have in front of me?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to this one and also in general.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In such cases when members of the public that I worked in go to the site then the report is compiled by the inspector from the department concerned, and in this case I was that inspector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have a look at P612, pages 5 -- or page 5 in the English and B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you will see the same date on the document. It's the same incident that is concerned. An on-site investigation was carried out in relation to the tram that was hit, tram designated as 268, and the signature is that of Mihajlo Pavlovic's. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber how it is that he compiled such an official report? And in that report he describes the events that concern the incident.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said, the local police station goes to the site. They are the first to go to the site. Policemen in uniform secure the site, and crime inspector Mr. Pavlovic, for example, would then go to the site. Mr. Pavlovic was part of the department at the time. And this criminal official would then -- crime official, rather, would contact us to tell us what was happening, to inform us about everything. This official report is an internal one that was compiled for that police station. It isn't sent to anyone else apart from the head of the police station. The report of mine that we had a look at a minute ago is important, and all other documents are based on it. All expert reports and so on are based on that document that is compiled in relation to the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In his report, Mr. Pavlovic says that at 12.30, at the same time as you, obtained information -- he obtained information that fire had been opened on this tram and the duty investigative judge was informed of the incident, and he then established an on-site investigation commission, and he doesn't say that the investigating judge was present at the site. Does this refresh your memory? Was the investigating judge at the site?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, the official report that I drafted on this occasion is authoritative, and since it says that the investigating judge was at the site, he therefore carried out or was involved in this on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So it wouldn't -- so what the official report drafted by Mr. Pavlovic says is not correct in this case.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says in Mr. Pavlovic's report is not something I can interpret, saying that the investigating judge wasn't present at the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're suggesting that there's a contradiction. Even if the Pavlovic report doesn't say that he was present, it also does not say that he was not present, does it? Or is -- or did I misunderstand your questions? Now, the final thing is if there's any suggestion that this report is false or fake or is -- there are lies on it, then please come to that point as quickly as possible and not purely on the basis that the report says that the duty investigating judge was notified and he formed an inquiry commission, and where it does not say that Mr. Pavlovic at no point in time was present at the scene of this incident, that's not a good basis for, and certainly not -- goes very much to the point of saying that the report is false, fake, inaccurate. It's all rather marginal as we understand it now and as presented by you. So if you want to make that stronger point, please do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to do that now, Your Honours. I just want to lay a foundation for the questions I would like to put to the witness. I think this is what is essential for these questions. Could we see P3, page 24. It's a bundle of photographs from Sarajevo -- of Sarajevo. And could the usher please give the witness a pen so that he can mark certain locations. Could we please zoom in to the central part. I'm interested in the yellow building. Could we zoom in a little more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise what we can see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a general view of the site where you carried out the investigation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see the site where I carried out the on -- investigation in this photograph. It's a little further to the east. But according to eyewitness statements, the location at which the tram was hit is visible in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for having clarified that. Could we now ask you to mark with an arrow the direction in which the tram was moving.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you mark with a circle the location where you noted the presence of the first tram that was hit? I'm referring to the first tram, number 268. Would I be right if I said that this street where the trams were present was called Zmaja od Bosne?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree that the Marsala Tita Street can't be seen in the area depicted by the photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it can't be seen there. It continues from Zmaja od Bosne Street and an investigation was carried out in Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber what the name of this transversal street was at the time, if you look to the right from the direction which the trams drive?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Franje Rackog street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that immediately behind the Zmaja od Bosne and Franje Rackog, the crossroads of those two street, the tram-lines turn to the right if you're looking in the direction which the trams advance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you. That is the so-called S curve.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And according to your recollection, could you tell me if the tram, tram 268, was hit before the S curve, in the S curve, or once it left the S curve?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The location where the tram was hit, this is something that we learned from eyewitnesses. In view of the fact that the investigation was carried out at the location where it was carried out I could give you a hypothetical answer to this very precise question of yours. I cannot give you a precise answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. So you don't know exactly where this happened other than what the information of the eyewitnesses was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at the same -- yes, but before we finish this technical part, all I would like to ask you is the following: Could you mark the circle with a T so that we can mark the place that eyewitnesses said that the tram was hit, and then in this form we could tender this document for adoption into the file of this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document as marked by the witness becomes D109, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Can we now look at P612 [Realtime transcript read in error "P162"] again in e-court, and can we look at page 4, both in the B/C/S and the English versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We can't really see it so well, but still I would like to ask you to look at it together with me. This is a document dated the 3rd of March, 1995, signed by the chief of the centre. I assume that it's the security services centre chief. His name is Enes Bezdorb. The document states in paragraph 3 that: "The on-site investigation established that about 1210 hours on the 3rd of March, 1995, at the junction of Marsala Tita and Franje Rackog Streets, a single bullet fired from aggressor positions at Grbavica hit tram number 268 ..." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dispatch was of course signed by the chief of security at the centre because he was the only one who could sign dispatches like this. On the other hand, the operatives were the ones who actually drafted the dispatches. As for the location where the Marsala Tita and Franje Rackog Streets meet or join, this is an error formally speaking; however, it's just an error involving a distance of some 10 to 15 metres. So formally Franje Rackog Street does not border Marsala Tita Street. However, Marsala Tita Street continues on to the Zmaja od Bosne Street some 10 metres farther than these crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because I'm going to show you some more documents, and then we will come back to the location from where the shot could have been fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at the same exhibit but page 8 of the B/C/S and page 9 of the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I think that this document was shown to you during the examination-in-chief. This is a report on the forensic on-site investigation which is a part of the case file that is sent to the Prosecutor's office related to this incident, which states that the location of the incident was at the intersection of the Franje Rackog and Marsala Tita Streets. So I'm asking you again do you still believe that the incident occurred some ten metres before that as you look in the direction of the movement of tram 268?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that I can say in relation to this is the following: I'm not sure even today that many citizens of Sarajevo know exactly where Zmaja od Bosne Street ends and Marsala Tita Street begins. So what I am stating and what I put in my report is that according to reports by eyewitnesses, the tram was hit at the location which I marked with a circle on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But would we agree that authorised officials such as the CSB chief and the crime investigation technician who drafts the documents following the search or the investigation on site are supposed to know where which street is when they provide these statements?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can agree with you about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, this is all rather argumentative. What you want to say is that what the document says may not be fully in accordance with what he -- what the witness now says. That point is clear to us, so let's move on. And apart from that I think page 34, line 7, reference is made to P162, where apparently we are looking at P612. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps I am mistaken, but we are actually looking at P612. Thank you. Can we now look at the same document, page 25 in the B/C/S and page 20 of the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, sir, you said in your official report you indicated the actual location on the basis of what eyewitnesses of this incident said, and we have a statement by one of the eyewitnesses. It was a person who was actually wounded on the occasion. Four days after the incident, he described the incident and stated when the tram was close to the containers between the Assembly of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Marin Dvor, he heard a shot and all the passengers in the tram, including him and Asima, dropped down or laid down on the floor - do you see that? - and according to this description can we agree that according to this eyewitness and the person who was wounded in the incident, the location where the tram was hit is at least 100 metres farther towards the east.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can agree with you that the position is somewhat more to the east than the one that I indicated, but not by 100 metres. Not by that much, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Why am I asking you all of these things? Would you agree with me that it's not the same if we're talking about precise measurements of the location where the bullet was fired -- actually, it's important to measure down not to 50 metres or 100 metres but down to a half metre in order to be able to measure precisely the angle of impact, and all of this is important in order to establish precisely the place where the projectile was fired from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we can agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is a long statement about what people should do rather than a question about facts, Mr. Stojanovic. Try -- let's try to focus on -- on facts rather than on whether the witness agrees that half a metre or 75 centimetres or 25 centimetres or 10 metres would be the best to measure. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, regarding this incident, did you have the opportunity to read the reports on the forensic examination of the site, and did you have the opportunity to look at the findings of the ballistics expert regarding the barrel size in relation to the entry and exit locations of the projectile that hit the tram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you said yourself at the beginning today, I really am not a ballistics expert. I'm not trained in ballistics examinations. It was not my job to conduct such examinations, so I'm not really the proper person to give you answers to these kind of questions or for these kind of analyses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your official report of the 3rd of March, 1995, you noted that the projectile was fired from the Grbavica area, and was this based on you having some more detailed information about the location from where the projectile was fired?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that location fire would usually be opened from the building which at that time was known as the Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when you know these -- this information about the Metalka building and the directions that were pointed out by the eyewitnesses to the incident, and if necessary we could go back to the picture because I don't want this to be any kind of trick question, but would you agree that the location described by the eyewitnesses, by the wounded person, could not have been hit from the Metalka building? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So much time has passed since then, so right now I'm really unable to give you a definitive answer to that question. I cannot say that it was impossible. It's more difficult to hit that than from the location that I marked on that photograph, but I cannot confirm your assertion that it was impossible even if it was that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at P3 once again, please, page 24. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in just for one octave. Could we zoom out, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the witness Gicevic, as we read a little bit earlier, said that according to his best recollection the shot occurred when the tram was between the B&H Assembly and Marin Dvor. I would like to ask you this: You've got the key on the photograph, so can we agree on the fact that the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina is this white building just in front of the building marked by the number 4 on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can we agree that the Marin Dvor area are the buildings which are across from the Assembly, and they're along the road that is Zmaja od Bosne Street?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's from the church that you can see on the photograph, and then it's to the right, to the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can we agree that the Metalka facility, the building, as you referred to it and that is marked in this photograph, is the building in the square marked with the number 8?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And is it possible, now that you can see this aerial photograph, to say that you could hit a tram from the Metalka building that happened to be in front of the B and H Assembly in the manner that you say the eyewitnesses described?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, was the BiH Assembly building the same at the time of the incident as it is now, to your knowledge? I'm not asking you to give testimony. Perhaps the witness could tell us. Was the building the same at the time of the incident as you now see it on these -- this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the same, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer to your question would be speculation. I said the first time I answered the question that I cannot really be precise. I cannot say yes, it could have been hit, and in the same way I cannot say it could not have been hit. It's just speculation. The statement by the eyewitness is authentic. There are other statements by witnesses who asserted something else. However, in my report, the location where the shot came from is not specifically mentioned. There is an assumption, but the place could not have been measured precisely from the position where we were conducting the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So can we're agree then that you as a professional performing an official task now and then, based on the information you obtained on the scene, could not even with close accuracy determine where the shot was fired from or precisely where the tram was when it was struck?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we were to rely exclusively on technical possibilities of answering your question, then, no, not a single tram -- for not a single tram was it possible to determine exactly the origin of fire, but there are certain other technical and expect, and I still stand by what my official report states, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any information according to which members of the ABiH had positions in the executive council building as well that we can see in photograph number 4, and in the Assembly building that you have located, and sometimes in the Unis building, which has been marked with number 5 in this photograph? Did you have any such information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said in answer to one of your previous questions, as a policeman, I didn't have any precise information about the locations at which the ABiH had positions. Given that the demarcation line was near, the front line was near, and the locations you have mentioned, apart from the Unis buildings which are quite far away, our locations where -- I wouldn't be surprised to learn that the ABiH had its own positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know in the course of your work that there were sniper nests, ABiH sniper nests, there, at least in the wider area that we are referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any such information. I still have no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you something about the person who was involved in ballistics reports, but before we identify the person, I'd just like to tell you the following: According to the documents we have -- according to the documents in my possession, forensic investigation of the vehicle was carried out. You were shown photographs, and you can see the bullet entry point. You can see where it came out on the right-hand side of the tram. And according to that information, the barrel was to the right flank of the tram, behind the tram --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want the Chamber to be able to follow all your reasoning, then, rather, take us to the photographs you are relying upon so that we can see it, because I'm lost already. "You were shown photographs." I think we have a whole series of photographs. "You can see the bullet entry point." I think we have two photographs with bullet entry points. So take us to the relevant material and we'll be better able to understand the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, could we please move into private session very briefly and then it won't perhaps be necessary to proceed in this manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see P612 again. I'd like to see page 19 in the B/C/S version and page 13 and 14 in the English version. First page 13 and then page 14. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you have already seen this document when you had the proofing for your testimony. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the documents that was shown to me -- that was shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that the person who drafted the document was someone whose name is Zlatko Medjedovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember having mentioned my colleague Medjedovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm mistaken but in that case, have a look at the document. Is the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's what the document says. I don't know whether there is any dispute about that but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, but it bears the signature of a different person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's signed on behalf of. So therefore I wouldn't expect the same person to sign, because otherwise you wouldn't write down "on behalf of." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since one name is printed but it bears a different signature under "for," I don't know who drafted it, but I do know that both these individuals are ballistics experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember who was with you in the course of the investigation, which one of the two, or were both of them present?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I think Medjedovic was there. I can't remember whether the other one was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll now show you some photographs, but, Your Honours, perhaps it might be a good time to have a break now, and then after the break I could go through these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then do I understand that you then finish in half an hour from there? Okay. We'll take a break, but we'll first move into closed session, and we'll remained in closed session until we have resumed after the break.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I'd just like to apologise on behalf of General Mladic for having started five minutes late.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, we have this document on the screen, the one we were dealing with before the break, and in the last paragraph it says that according to the ballistics expert, the position of the mouth of the barrel at the time the projectile was fired was to the right of the tram and behind the tram, at the rear. It says the direction from which the fire was shot was from behind the front, from the right to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we have a look at P612, page 12 in the B/C/S version, and it's the same page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And let's briefly go through -- through this. Is this a photograph that shows the point of entry of the bullet, the point at which it penetrated the side of the tram?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the photograph in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have a look at page 6 -- I mean page 16 in the B/C/S version, and it's page 12 in the English version. We can stay on page 12 in the English version. We have the text here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we agree that number 2 marks the position hit by the bullet on the other side of the tram, or is that the same side of the tram that we are dealing with, the side of the tram that you referred to in your official report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficulty to me -- for me to be sure about this photograph. I can't answer your question on the basis of this photograph. I can't say whether this is where the bullet entered on the same side of the tram or whether it was on the other side of the tram.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, let's first check which part of the English page covers this photograph. Let me -- is that "Interior of the tram, garage number 268, with traces marked with the numbers 2 and 3," in the middle? Is that the one?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's text, Your Honours. Photograph number 6. So it's the sixth comment, if you're looking at the English testing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see "Traces marked with the numbers 2 and three, photographed at closer range." That is what we're looking at at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's conclude. You cannot say for certain here today whether the position marked with number 2 is the other side, the opposite side of the tram or is this the photograph from the inside of the tram of the site at which the bullet entered the tram number 268.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the entrance, but I can't say for certain on the basis of this photograph, but I do think that this is the point of entry of the bullet that penetrated that side of the tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's have a look at photograph P3 again. It's page 24. And then to the best of your recollection, I would like to ask you to mark this photograph, to mark the place where Zmaja od Bosne Street turns into the Marsala Tita Street, the location at which these two streets intersect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To start with, could we zoom in to have a better picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you could mark this photograph with a transversal line in relation to the Zmaja od Bosne Street. Could you mark the location of the intersection, or in fact could you mark the location in which Marsala Tita Street starts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain, but I think that this location can't be seen by the building that is now the building of the joint institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It's perhaps at the first third of these buildings where the buildings of the institutions are now located.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now according to what we see, what you're describing, if we look at the Metalka building, the place where Zmaja od Bosne becomes Titova Street, if the tram were in that location, could that shot have come from the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can answer that question, please do so. But on the basis of these kind of photographs, Mr. Stojanovic, without a position from where the photograph is taken exactly at the point from where you say it could or could not have a line of sight, that is -- the Chamber does not accept that as a possibility, unless the witness has any other explanation on why he thinks he could do it. But on the basis of these kind of photographs, it's just impossible to do it, apart from any inaccuracies that may exist in other respects, but please proceed.
