Witness, if you can answer the question, please do so. If not, Mr. Stojanovic, you're invited to put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I cannot add anything to what you have already said. I'm really not able to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In that case, can we now please look at P3, photograph that is on page 25. This is the next photograph in the e-court system. Thank you. Can we please look at the photograph on the left-hand side. It's a close-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this aerial photograph provides a view of the Franje Rackog and Zmaja od Bosne intersection and the Metalka building that you talked about but now looking from the position of the Holiday Inn Hotel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that you can see on the Zmaja od Bosne Street clear traces of tram rails which at one point separate off? And if we look at that from the direction that tram 268 was moving, this forks off to the right. Do you see that on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I -- I can see that on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that you didn't know when you mentioned that the possible direction of fire from the Metalka building from Grbavica, you were unable to say from which part of the building the shot could have been fired? You simply don't know that, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And also, you don't know after Grbavica was reintegrated, which is how you put it, and after investigations were conducted in this area the Metalka, you did not actually go to the Metalka building and conduct an investigation there in order to be able to determine the location from where the fire came?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I personally did not go to inspect that particular building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to put the last question to you relating to this incident. The question is: Do you recall that that day at that time there was an incident, and there was firing between a patrol of the French battalion and units at positions around the Miljacka river in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is stated in my official report, and if I recall correctly, there was an exchange of fire that day between the French and the -- and that fire was opened from positions of the Army of Republika Srpska and those of the French battalion, but this is something you would need to check in the report, but I think that that's what happened around that time when this tram incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. I don't have to show you the official report. I am satisfied that this is stated in your report. Now I'm going to put this question to you: You assert that if the bullet did come from the Metalka building, according to the ballistics expert's findings, it could have only have had come from there if the tram was exactly at the Zmaja od Bosne and the Franje Rackog intersection. It could not have happen in the way that Witness Gicevic described, and it could not have been in the way that it was described in the dispatch. Would I be correct? This is what we, the Defence, assert.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm unable to give you a precise answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I will not be dealing with this topic anymore. Could we briefly just turn to the events of the 23rd of November, 1994, which you also investigated. Do you recall that you were questioned about this incident during the examination-in-chief in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not sure that I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I will try to reformulate it and to make it simpler. Am I correct that on the 24th of November, 1994, you investigated, as the leader of a team, one incident that struck another tram that was going along that same street?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at P614 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is your report, and I'm just going to ask you if you can remember if you know, according to the people who are in charge of these duties in your investigation team, where this bullet came from.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that according to eyewitness statements, I haven't found it yet in the report, but as far as I can remember, I think they refer to these four skyscrapers in Grbavica, but I would really need to look at the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was this sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we talk about incidents that occurred in Sarajevo as a result of firearms, it's very difficult to assess whether they were explosive sniper weapons or some other kind of infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we look at page 2 of this document in both versions. And in those documents you state that at 1545 hundred hours, tram number 238 was hit while moving towards the new part of town, towards the west. And the tram was hit in the stretch of Zmaja od Bosne Street running from the Philosophy Faculty to the museum. Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that you didn't provide any more detailed information about the type of weapon and that you describe the location as being from the south to the south-east or south-west, I don't see which one, in relation to the spot where the tram was hit from the direction of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And what I want to ask you now is this, and this is from document P619. Can we see that in e-court, please. And while we're waiting I would just like you to confirm the following: Is this the incident that you established as the one where no traces of bullet could be found because the bullet entered through an open window?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not sure why in the English version there is a part that is blacked out, but I will ask you this: Do you recall that one of the eyewitnesses at the time said that the tram was hit by a burst of fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when we had cases like this, my colleagues would interview witnesses. These colleagues were from other departments, so if you asked me if some witness said that the tram was hit by bursts of fire, then what I can say is no, at this moment I cannot recall whether anybody said that or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because we have the official report in front of us, and in paragraph 2 of the report, and you can see that for yourself, it is noted that according to a statement by an eyewitness, Mr. Tanovic [as interpreted], he heard a burst of automatic gunfire, and then after that she felt a blow in her shoulder and heard glass shattering. My question is this: Do you agree that this eyewitness statement is opposite of what you actually found on the site, and that is that the bullet entered through an open window?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is opposite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: To the extent that the witness said he was testifying about the incident when the bullet entered the open window, I believe that the Defence should first direct the witness to the first paragraph in this statement and be careful not to confuse the two different trams that were hit in this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, there seems to be a clear problem if this statement here says that the window was shattered and at the same time to say that this is the same incident as with a bullet entering through an open window. That should be clarified first before we draw further conclusions. Could you please follow the suggestion of Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will, Your Honour. I think I already tried that with the question whether this tram is from that same incident but I will try to be a bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your official report it states that on that day, two trams were hit, one at 1530 [Realtime transcript read in error "1535"] hundred hours, that's tram 263, and then 15 minutes later, tram 238 moving in the same direction was also hit. And this is why I asked you whether the indent that involved 238, the one when the bullet entered through the open window, was the one involving tram 238.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. As you yourself said, there were two trams. The first one was hit through an open window, and this was not the case with the second tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to end with this question that was also put to you by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at P618.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just before you move to the next, just a clarification for the record, Mr. Stojanovic. At page 54, line 4, you said one at -- one was hit at 1535 hundred hours, but in the document it was 1530 hundred hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you for your intervention. It was at 1530 hundred hours, and that is what the official report also states. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So this is just what I wanted to clarify. In this report that was shown to you and for which you said during the examination-in-chief, if you recall, that this is probably an error here by the person who wrote the report, tram 263 that is mentioned in the report and for which it is said that the rear right side glass of the front car was damaged, could that be actually something that applies to tram 238, and could this perhaps be a typing error?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect, I'm really unable to deal with such details. I would like to be specific and precise, but I cannot in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank the witness. I would like to thank the Trial Chamber. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Ms. Harbour, any need to put further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Just very few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, at temporary transcript page 10 today, there was a discussion about your 1995 statement, which is P609, and paragraph 14, and this was regarding the second round of shelling on Livanjska Street on the 8th of November, 1994, and you were asked: "In it statement, is it true that the conclusion you drew is that one shell fell, not two?" And you responded: "What you are saying is correct. All I can do is assume that I was referring to the second shell because it had certain consequences. As for the shell that hit the ground, that was embedded in the ground. There were no consequences." I would like to make it very clear to the Chamber what actually happened that day in this second round of shelling, so I'm going to show you the official report that you drafted, which is P622?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If we could go to the bottom of page 1 in the English, and it's about three-fourths of the way down in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Now, the very last line in the English, and it's near the end in the -- in your version, states: "On 8 November 1994, at around 1725 hours a mortar shell fell and exploded on the asphalt road surface across the road from house number 36 in Livanjska Street, killing one person." And if we could please have the next page in the English, although it's on the same page in the original. The very first line reads: "On the same day, at around 1730 hours, another mortar shell fell in the yard of house number 36 in Livanjska Street, slightly wounding one person." Does this report accurately reflect the situation you investigated, Mr. Miokovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Moving on to the next topic, at transcript page 18 and 19 from today, there was a discussion about whether a criminal report was submitted with regard to the first shelling on Livanjska Street on the 8th of November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And I would like to call up 65 ter 28606. And, Your Honours, I will mention that this I am bringing up directly in response to the cross-examination. This document is not on our 65 ter list, but it was disclosed to the Defence in batch 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. I've heard of no objections on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, do you recognise what this document is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a criminal report that was submitted in relation to the consequences of the first shelling on the 8th of March [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: 8th of -- you said the 8th of March. Did you mean to say the 8th of March?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said November.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could I tender this report into evidence, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28606 becomes Exhibit P624, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: For completeness of the record, I would also like to tender the criminal report that was shown to the witness related to the second shelling on Livanjska Street, and that is now uploaded as 65 ter 12942B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of any objections, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 12942B becomes Exhibit P625, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Miokovic, we have discussed the fact that Zmaja od Bosne Street turns into Marsala Tita Street and I would like to know from you does Franje Rackog Street intersect with the tram-line and the street that the tram-line runs down at more than one location?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I have understood your question correctly, Franje Rackog Street does not intersect the tram-line. It merges with the Zmaja od Bosne Street, but it does not intersect the tram-lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Let me rephrase. Does Franje Rackog Street intersect with the street on which the tram-line runs, whether it's Zmaja od Bosne or Marsala Tita? Does it insect with that street at more than one point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIOKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a problem with the interpretation. No. It intersects it only at one location.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Harbour. Mr. Stojanovic, any further questions related to -- in relation to the re-examination of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then just for me to better understand, Mr. Stojanovic, you were suggesting that there may be an error somewhere in the description of the two tram incidents, the one involving tram 263 and the other one, 238. That's at least what I understood from your questions, although it's not entirely clear to me. You asked our attention for a witness saying that the window was completely demolished, whether that was the same tram as the tram with the open window through which the bullet entered, and it was not entirely clear to me what you meant, because what the witness describes relates to tram 238. Now, the description of a tram where no damage was found to the glass was a description of tram 263. Now, it was not entirely clear to me where you suggested there may have been an error.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm referring to document P618 in relation to which the witness said in the course of the examination-in-chief that he considered there to be an error in the document. In that document which you'll have in front of you now, it says that when the incident involving tram 263 is related, well, we have determined that that is the tram that was hit by a bullet which entered through an open window, and in that document it says -- this isn't the right document. It's P618.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at that, because I want to try to understand all the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the right document, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document, the technician who drafted the document stated with regard to tram 263, and in relation to that tram, if the witness agrees, we have determined that that is the tram that was hit by a bullet through an open window. And the conclusion that was drawn in relation to that tram is that the bullet entered through the rear windowpane on the right side, and the witness confirmed that the tram was heading from the east to the west and that the bullet could only have been fired from the south, that is to say from the left-hand side of that tram. I'm not sure whether I have been clear enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that, but I still do not see -- that is a comment on what is described for tram 263. That doesn't say a word about tram 238. So, therefore, I'm confused what -- what consequences it would have for the accuracy of where the witness says for tram 238 that the window was broken. It's unclear to me, but if that is how you explained your questions, I'll have to do it with that. We have no further questions for you, Witness. Therefore, I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you both by the parties and be the Bench, and I wish you, Mr. Miokovic, a safe return home again. Before you leave the courtroom, we turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for a short while.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Bolton, you have an opportunity to address the Court. I think you asked for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. There are two different issues I'd like to address the Court on, and the first is with respect to some of the housekeeping matters arising after General Fraser completed his evidence. Your Honour, you asked us to prepare a redacted statement for the public of General Fraser's statement, and that is now available and has been uploaded, and with the Court's permission, if we could release that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have a number for it or --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. It's 28590A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it is exactly what?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: It is General Fraser's amalgamate the statement and you will recall there was one issue in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: That that paragraph -- entire paragraph has been redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- the new version, then, can replace the old one that was about protected information, family relations.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, the new version, the redacted version can replace the unredacted version.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Secondly, Your Honours, there was -- you will recall after the 92 ter procedure with General Fraser, I moved for the admission of all the exhibits with the exception of three exhibits, and I understand that the exhibits had -- that weren't contested have been assigned provisional exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the others have been assigned provisional exhibit numbers as well, but the three that were objected to you said you would come to them later.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. My information was that the ones that had been given provisional exhibit numbers had also been MFI'd, and I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They were all MFI'd. We'll decide on admission. Those not objected to of course we'll admit, but then three are remaining. The first one is 65 ter 8735, which has been provisionally assigned number P588.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. With respect to that document, I should indicate with respect to all three documents it's the Prosecution's position that they meet the test for admission as associated exhibits, and in particular, that they would meet the test -- the lower of the two standards being that they would render -- their exclusion would render of lower probative value the witness's statement. The first of those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should we first identify all three of them so we know for sure what we are talking about. The first one as I said was 65 ter 8735. The second one is 65 ter 9741, and I think the third one is 65 ter 11189.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: That's my understanding, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. These three you say they meet the standard for admission.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. And dealing with -- so with respect to 65 ter 11189, my only submission is that it meets the test for admission as an associated exhibit. With respect to 08735, it's my respectful submission that some of the evidence that was a tendered through the witness provides additional corroboration of the authenticity and reliability of this document. This was, to remind Your Honours, a VRS Main Staff order that had been signed by General Milovanovic, and the issue was who controlled -- we would say it indicates that the freedom of movement for the UN and UNPROFOR was controlled at the level of the Main Staff of the VRS. That is what the witness has indicated in his statement at -- I believe it's paragraph, I think, 130 or 132. That evidence, in my respectful submission, was corroborated by the re-examination of General Fraser, and in particular, the re-examination on Defence document 1D00474. That was a SRK document which the Defence put to the witness, and in that document there is -- I read a portion of it to the witness regarding freedom of movement of the UN where General Galic had emphasised that that was an issue not in his competence and proposed the issue be resolved at the highest level as part of the overall problem of Sarajevo. So in my respectful submission, that portion of the document is further corroboration of the contents of the proposed associated exhibit and enhances its reliability and authenticity. And finally, Your Honours, with respect to 65 ter 09741, it's discussed at paragraph 134 of the witness's amalgamated statement, and it's a document again signed by General Milovanovic, dated the 12th of June, addressed to the Ilidza Brigade and indicating that it is the VRS Main Staff that decides on the use of aerial bombs and not -- and possibly a corps if the VRS GS approves and not a brigade according to its plan. And it's my respectful submission that the contents of this document and its reliability are corroborated by two exhibits that were introduced through General Fraser, being Exhibits P580 and P581. And P581, Your Honours may recall was a letter - or I would characterise it as a correspondence, I guess - from General Mladic to Colonel Tadija where he was questioning a planned use of modified air bombs, asking questions about who had authorised it, and reminding him that he needed the approval of either the level of the Main Staff or if it had been issued by the commander, the supreme commander, he wanted to know. So in my respectful submission again, that document corroborates the authenticity of the proposed associated exhibit. Those are my submissions with respect to the admissibility of the exhibits, Your Honour. Do you wish me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should we try to deal with this first, because these were the three objected to by the Defence. I don't think, but forgive me when I'm wrong, that we have received yet the reasons for the objection, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, apart from the very general objections that were in the response to the Rule 92 ter motion, if I can begin, I guess, with 08735, I have here, Your Honours, that the witness has not given any personal testimony as to any personal knowledge of this particular document, and it is dated before the witness assumed his position as MA in sector Sarajevo. With regard to 09741, although it is during the time period when the witness was present in Sector Sarajevo, the statement and the testimony of the witness have not added anything to the document. He cannot authenticate a document that is not signed by him and for which there is no testimony that he received or was aware of the document during the relevant time period. With respect to 11189, this is again a document that purports to be of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and therefore the witness would not have been a signator to it. It is not discussed by the witness and does not -- he does not add any personal knowledge to this document. So, again, those are the bases for the objections to these three documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will consider the submission by the parties and then decide on admissibility. Apart from that since the others were not objected, provisionally assign exhibits to which provisionally were assigned numbers P590 up to and including P602, and next range, P604 up to and including P607 are admitted into evidence. Ms. Bolton, there was another matter which you would like to make submissions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: There is, Your Honour. Just before we leave this area, just so there's no misunderstanding, the unredacted statement admitted under seal from General Fraser has been assigned an exhibit number, and we -- we do wish to rely on that for the Trial Chamber's deliberations at the end of the day. So we would need a separate P number for the public version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think -- but -- but let me -- I think I'm now back on track again on this matter. It's not a matter of replacing the evidence. The evidence remains as it was before. I don't think, but we'll check that, that new exhibit numbers would be assigned to public versions of the same evidence, but we'll deal with that. It's clear that there is now a version available which is ready to -- for the public, and we'll deal with that together with Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Yes. So the other issue I would like to address Your Honours on, and I thank you for the opportunity to do so, has to do with some issues that arose primarily at the beginning of General Fraser's testimony last week on the 5th of December. And I think, Your Honour Justice Orie, you correctly indicated at one point that I seemed to be taken aback or somewhat dismissive of the Defence's complaints with respect to the -- the addition of that one exhibit to the 65 ter list, and I think that that was fair criticism, Your Honour, but I'd like to perhaps indicate that there is some area of confusion for the Prosecution, and it would be helpful to us if we could clear up that area. So there were two issues that were raised at the very beginning of General Fraser's testimony by the Defence, and they both pertain to an e-mail that I had sent on the 2nd of December, 2012, which I copied the Trial Chamber on, and that was an e-mail indicating that the existing 65 ter summary for the witness didn't include three topics, and also that there were two additional potential exhibits that I intended to present to the witness during proofing and that I might possibly seek to introduce them through the witness. And at the beginning of proceedings, the objections raised by the Defence were to first -- they were of the opinion that we had not complied with the Chamber's guideline with respect to the amendment of the 65 ter summary; and secondly, that we had not complied with the guidance with respect to the addition of exhibits after the seven-day guidance rule. And specifically at page 5765, the Defence stated: "Defence notes that it received an e-mail on Sunday, December the 2nd, 2012, at 6.35 p.m. for this witness with three now topics for the 65 ter summary and two new 65 ter documents of exhibits. This is not more than a couple of days before the testimony of the witness, and this testimony has been scheduled for at least two months." With respect, Your Honour, to the 65 ter summary, your guidance of the 24th of August, 2012, at page 1638 indicated that the purpose of Rule 65 ter witness summaries is to notify the opposing party and the Chamber of the content of evidence expected to be elicited from a witness. Such notice should be given sufficiently in advance of a witness's testimony so as to enable the opposing party to prepare for the witness's cross-examination. When amendments to the 65 ter summary concern information which was included in the witness statement was filed per the 92 ter motion, the Chamber will consider that the Defence has been on notice sufficiently in advance of the witness's testimony of the Prosecution's intention to lead the proposed additional evidence which is included in the 92 ter statement. The e-mail I sent on the 2nd of December, 2012, indicated that the existing 65 ter summary for General Fraser didn't include references to modified air bombs, targeting, or the witness's personal observations of General Mladic. However, I expressly stated repeatedly in the e-mail that these were issues that were addressed in the witness's amalgamated statement, and I provided paragraph references to those portions of the amalgamated statement. And my intention, in fact, in sending this e-mail was to avoid the very situation that arose, which was to avoid any suggestion that these were new areas, and so I was a little taken aback when having taken -- or made the effort to avoid the situation that it did arise, and I apologise, because I obviously displayed that annoyance, and I did not intend to. I try never to lose patience in court or to display emotion, and so I do apologise to the extent that I was not successful in doing so. And I certainly can understand why the Trial Chamber was critical of my tone of voice when responding to those areas of inquiry. The second issue raised is the area where I think there may be some confusion with respect to the existing guidance from the Prosecution's perspective at least, and I think in fact the Defence has also indicated in their submission on this issue that there may be misunderstanding as to what is required. In that e-mail I've averred to, I had indicated I intended to present the witness with two documents that I had not included on the list of potential exhibits that was disclosed to the Defence seven days before the start of General Fraser's testimony. These were documents that are not discussed in the witness's statement or have never been discussed in his prior evidence. They're not documents he authored, and so I didn't know whether or not he'd be able to identify the documents or to speak to their contents. And in including this information in the e-mail, again I thought I was adhering with the guidance, which on the 4th of September, 2012, indicated this with respect to the sending of the list of documents. This is at transcript page 2160, for the record: "The Defence sought guidance from the Chamber about when such list of documents used by the Prosecution with witnesses should be sent. The Chamber will not set any strict time limits in this respect at this stage and is confident that the parties can find common ground on this issue without involving the Chamber. At the same time, the parties are encouraged to send lists of documents to be used during examination-in-chief as early as possible. The Chamber would expect that a first list of documents be sent no later than seven days prior to the witness's testimony. Such a list could then be complemented at a later stage following any proofing of the witness." The way the Prosecution interprets this guidance is that we should include all documents on our seven-day list that we know may be introduced through the witness. So documents that we already know the witness can speak to but that the guidance allows for the possibility that a limited number of addition documents may be added after proofing and whether or not that is allowed will depend on whether there is any actual prejudice to the Defence, and that's an issue that must be determined on a case-by-case basis. And it is our respectful submission that this is the only interpretation of your guidance that would be consistent with the Rules, because the adoption of a hard and fast rule that prohibited the Prosecution from relying on documents that weren't included on its seven-day list would amount to a finding of prejudice any time such documents were included and wouldn't involve any case by case analysis of whether there was actual prejudice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bolton, you have used now 20 minutes approximately on a matter you said you would deal with in 10 minutes. Let me try to cut matters short, because I think that you have dealt with the -- what the specific document was about, I'm not talking about the adding to the 65 ter summary at this moment because that's something that finally did not -- was not the focus of -- and was not the basis for our decision. It was a document, a handwritten document, documentation about a modified air bomb which landed in Hrasnica. That was a document which consisted of two parts: The first part a general description of that bomb falling there, and the second a -- detailed sketches, et cetera, on all kind of particles of that bomb that were found. Now, if the modified air bomb was part of a specific section of the witness's statement, and it was, five or six paragraph, and where the Hrasnica incident was the only specific incident referred to, there was another one but without any further specifics, then the Chamber would have expected that the -- the Prosecution would have foreseen that the Hrasnica incident was part of the evidence to be given by that witness, and it was. We have two other documents, one preparing for, another one reporting about this air bomb being -- this projectile being fired. Under those circumstances, the Chamber had difficulties in understanding why it was only during proofing that a far more detailed report about the landing of that air bomb would suddenly have come up from the blue of the sky and suddenly turned out to be relevant where its relevance was perfectly clear on from the beginning. Second, if you intended to use it only to establish that that modified air bomb fell there, there was no need to do that, because there were already -- there was one other, even an insider document which confirmed that. We fired it. That is where it was. If, however, you wanted to use it for the technical details, pages and pages of small sketches, then of course it would be prejudicial for the Defence not to be aware of that, because they might want to consult experts on these specific small drawings, sketches, et cetera. Now, you didn't ask any question to the witness about those details, so therefore we take it that it was only that you intended to use it primarily and perhaps even exclusively for that modified air bomb having landed where the SRK -- the, yes, SRK report already says that it was fired and that's where it landed. So under those circumstances, the Chamber did not fully understand why that had not come up any earlier, and if you're interpreting our guidance and if you say, We understand it that you can add on the basis of proofing, then you should also understand that the Chamber expects the Prosecution to present a first list with all reasonably to be expected documents on that risk, leaving it open that something new may come up. But the Chamber had some difficulties in understanding that this was entirely new and could not be foreseen. That is the gist of what it is, and this is, as you may have noticed by now, is expressed on this case by case considerations. If there's anything further you'd like to say about it, again you asked for ten minutes. We have now spent 20 minutes, even 25 minutes on it. You may make further submissions on the matter, but you now know in more detail what -- what triggered, more or less, the focus on this document. At the same time, Mr. Ivetic, of course, since the details of that document have not been used in any way by the Prosecution, the mere fact that the modified air bomb landed in that area without further details, is there any dispute about that? Is there any prejudice inflicted on the Defence if we leave apart the sketches and the further details?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't believe there is a dispute as to that fact. The dispute was as to getting the document and all this other information through a witness who would not have the ability to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the parties are invited to see to what extent they can agree on admission of either the whole or a portion of that document into evidence or to agree, for example, on the fact that the modified air bomb landed at that point in time exactly at that spot. We take a break. If there is any need for further submissions, we'll hear from the parties. If the parties agree on anything the Chamber will hear from that from the parties on that matter. We need the next break also to prepare for the protective measures for the next witness. We take a break and we resume at 5 minutes to 2.00, and we only have limited time after that, only 20 more minutes to start the examination of the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Technical difficulties are there which we'll have to discuss in closed session. Therefore, and just to inform the public, there's hardly any chance that there will be any substantial hearing of evidence further today. We have to move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Shin, I'd like to deal with two matters briefly. First, you know that the Chamber has adopted in its guidance a reduction of the number of associated exhibits. To the extent possible, would you please consider or reconsider whether all the documents, all the associated exhibits on your list, whether you really need them, and then inform the Chamber accordingly. That is one. The second one is that on your list, non-associated exhibits and associated exhibits, we find two times 65 ter number 8139. The range of ERN numbers is for both the same, which already requires further clarification as to whether it's an associated exhibit or a non-associated exhibit, but perhaps even more important, the description of the documents, although bearing the same ERN numbers, is quite different. If I only look at the date the associated exhibit being of the 19th of February, 1994, whereas the non-associated with exactly the same ERN numbers, the 16 of August, 1994, and apart from that also different descriptions, different persons involved. Could you please make sure that this be clarified before we start with the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. If I may just briefly address those points. It was indeed my intention to revisit the issue of the associated exhibits in courtroom as we had indicated rather than do a reply brief on the first point, and I would be pleased to do that tomorrow. The -- on Your Honour's second point, yes, we had sent an e-mail noting that we had recognised an error but we will confirm that and be in a position to clarify that this afternoon. The -- just a quick look, myself, and being familiar with this list, of course, is that the document was intended to be proposed as an associated exhibit, and this additional entry on the non-associated exhibit will be deleted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then the description is the correct one, the remaining description is the correct one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Still with same ERN numbers, still quite alarming, but at least resolved for this moment for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise for that error, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I suggest that we adjourn for the day. Who will be -- Mr. Ivetic, you'll cross-examine the witness. Is there any other matter in relation to what we just -- nothing. Then we adjourn for the day, but not until after you've read the little note just passed to you by your client, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Our client is just again reiterating the objection to the protective measures sought for this witness as I believe we have already set forth in the filing that we made on 23 November, 2012.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As you may have noticed, they have been imposed in other cases. We're not free to just change them, only if we have reasons to do so, and after consultation with the other Chamber we would be in a position to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is on the record, that Mr. Mladic objects to the protective measures. We adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 11th of December, at 9.00 in the morning but uncertain yet in which courtroom we'll be. We stand adjourned.
